## Overview

This tutorial accompanies `selectFiberseqLociWorkflow` 0.99.1 or later and
follows the [function-reference tutorial](https://crystalshann.github.io/plot_selected_Fiber-seq_loci/function-reference.html) format:
function tables, executable examples, plots, and result exports.

**Leiden clustering** and **autocorrelation** have separate sections below.
Leiden groups reads by their m6A patterns. Autocorrelation describes repeating
patterns within each read as a function of distance in base pairs. ACF profiles
can also be clustered with their own independent Leiden analysis.

| Analysis | Input features | Controls | Result location |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Manhattan-distance Leiden | Observed m6A sites or bins | `clustering`, `window_size`, `k_neighbors`, `resolution`, `seed` | Locus `colData$cluster` and `metadata$clustering` |
| Autocorrelation | All consecutive bases in the locus | `autocorrelation`, `max_lag` | Separate ACF experiment with lags in rows |
| Optional ACF clustering | PCA of the ACF profiles | ACF `clustering`, `n_pcs`, `n_neighbors`, `resolution`, `seed` | ACF `colData$acf_cluster` and ACF metadata |

The two top-level switches are independent. They use the **same sample sheet**.
ACF settings do not change the m6A assay, read order or Manhattan cluster labels.

### Functions used

| Function | What it does |
|:--|:--|
| `make_sample_sheet()` / `prepare_regions()` | Define the shared inputs. |
| `analyze_loci()` | Extract full-span reads; optionally run either analysis. |
| `locus_autocorrelation()` | Compute ACF on an existing locus without rereading tracks. |
| `autocorrelation_profile()` | Report means, SD, SEM and valid/invalid read counts. |
| `plot_autocorrelation()` | Draw mean curves or a per-read heatmap. |
| `write_autocorrelation_results()` | Export the ACF experiment, tables and PDFs. |
| `write_locus_results()` | Export locus results and any attached ACF results. |

## Before you start

Install version 0.99.1 or later of the package following its README. The extra
R packages `uwot` and `irlba` are needed only for ACF clustering. This tutorial
uses them in the worked clustering examples. Python is not required.

```{r install-optional, eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("uwot", "irlba"))
```

```{r libraries}
library(selectFiberseqLociWorkflow)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
library(GenomicRanges)
stopifnot(packageVersion("selectFiberseqLociWorkflow") >= "0.99.1")
stopifnot(requireNamespace("uwot", quietly = TRUE),
          requireNamespace("irlba", quietly = TRUE))
```

### Download the synthetic test

Download these two files into the same directory:

- [R Markdown tutorial](autocorrelation-tutorial.Rmd)
- [Synthetic test dataset (ZIP)](synthetic-autocorrelation.zip)

The ZIP contains two bgzip/tabix BED12 m6A tracks, their indexes, a relative-path
sample sheet, a region table, ground-truth labels, checksums, and the complete
R generator. This is **entirely synthetic**, freely reusable data (CC0-1.0), not
an extract of the LCL samples. It contains 50 reads over a 2,000-bp artificial
locus: 24 with planted 180-bp spacing, 24 with planted 220-bp spacing, and two
zero-call controls. Both libraries contain both periodicities. This simplified
model demonstrates ACF behavior; it is not a biological nucleosome simulation.
The package's existing `example_data()` contains real LCL tracks, so it is not
used as the synthetic test here.

Knit with the default `run_lcl: false` anywhere the package is installed. The
real example needs access to the project's saved LCL input and report files:

```{r render-examples, eval=FALSE}
# Synthetic example only: no LCL files required.
rmarkdown::render("autocorrelation-tutorial.Rmd")

# Include the real LCL analysis on the project filesystem.
rmarkdown::render("autocorrelation-tutorial.Rmd",
    params = list(run_lcl = TRUE, project = "/project/spott/cshan/fiber-seq"))
```

`synthetic_zip` can point to a ZIP elsewhere. Set `output_dir` to a new or empty
folder to retain exports; the default uses a temporary directory. To select
another existing LCL run, edit `lcl_run` and `lcl_region` in the YAML header.
The values used to produce this page are recorded here:

```{r settings}
knitr::kable(data.frame(setting = c("package_version", "run_lcl", "lcl_region"),
    value = c(as.character(packageVersion("selectFiberseqLociWorkflow")),
              params$run_lcl, params$lcl_region)))
run_dir <- if (is.null(params$output_dir)) tempfile("acf-tutorial-results-") else
    path.expand(params$output_dir)
if (file.exists(run_dir) && (!dir.exists(run_dir) ||
    length(list.files(run_dir, all.files = TRUE, no.. = TRUE))))
    stop("Choose a new or empty output_dir")
dir.create(run_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

## Prepare the shared synthetic inputs

### Unzip and verify the files

The archive keeps paths relative to `samples.tsv`, so the download is portable.
The code extracts to a new temporary directory each time it runs.

```{r synthetic-inputs}
stopifnot(file.exists(params$synthetic_zip))
data_dir <- tempfile("acf-synthetic-input-")
dir.create(data_dir)
unzip(params$synthetic_zip, exdir = data_dir)
data_dir <- file.path(data_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation")
checksums <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "checksums.tsv"))
stopifnot(identical(unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(data_dir, checksums$file))),
                    checksums$md5))
samples <- make_sample_sheet(file.path(data_dir, "samples.tsv"))
regions <- prepare_regions(read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "regions.tsv")),
    coordinate_system = "bed")
validate_inputs(samples, regions)
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(samples)[, c("sample_name", "sample_label", "m6a_format")])
regions
```

The synthetic BED interval `[1000, 3000)` becomes `chrSynthetic:1001-3000`
in one-based inclusive coordinates. Every retained read spans the whole locus.
Zero-call reads remain in the assay. No footprint tracks are supplied.

## Leiden clustering {#leiden}

### Fit Manhattan-distance Leiden on the synthetic reads

This section uses only the existing m6A clustering path. The settings here
are separate from the ACF settings in the next section.

```{r leiden-fit}
leiden_results <- analyze_loci(samples, regions,
    clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = FALSE,
    window_size = 0, k_neighbors = 10, resolution = 1, seed = 1)
x_leiden <- leiden_results[[1]]
metadata(x_leiden)$clustering_status
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(sample = colData(x_leiden)$sample_label,
    cluster = colData(x_leiden)$cluster)))
```

```{r leiden-plots, fig.height=7}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_locus(x_leiden, "heatmap", clustered = TRUE))
```

```{r leiden-profile, fig.height=4}
plot_locus(x_leiden, "profile", clustered = TRUE)
```

Manhattan clustering compares calls at corresponding genomic positions.
Different periodicities and shifts can influence these clusters. The planted
periods are not labels supplied to the fitting algorithm, and they do not
require a particular number of Manhattan clusters.

## Autocorrelation {#autocorrelation}

### `locus_autocorrelation()` — compute per-read ACFs

Compute ACF on the exact locus already used above. No input files are reread.
`max_lag = 500` returns 501 features: lag zero through lag 500. Lag zero is one
for a nonconstant read. Curves omit lag zero by default so other lags are easier
to see. Constant reads have undefined (`NA`) ACF values.

```{r acf-compute}
a <- locus_autocorrelation(x_leiden, max_lag = 500)
stopifnot(identical(colnames(a), colnames(x_leiden)),
          identical(colData(a)$cluster, colData(x_leiden)$cluster))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(a)$acf_status)))
head(rowData(a))
```

For a mean-centered binary read, ACF at lag *k* is the sum of products between
bases *k* apart, divided by the fixed lag-zero sum of squares. The package uses
`stats::acf()` with no smoothing and no lag-dependent overlap correction.
All consecutive bases enter the calculation, including positions without calls.

### `autocorrelation_profile()` — summarize valid reads

```{r acf-summary}
profile <- autocorrelation_profile(a, group_by = "sample")
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(profile[profile$lag_bp %in% c(0, 180, 220), ]), digits = 4)
stopifnot(sum(colData(a)$acf_valid) == 48L,
          sum(!colData(a)$acf_valid) == 2L)
```

Means exclude constant reads; `n_reads`, `n_valid` and `n_invalid` make that
exclusion visible. SD and SEM are `NA` with fewer than two valid reads.
Both samples contain both periodicities, so their mean curves should be similar.

### `plot_autocorrelation()` — curves and heatmap

```{r acf-sample-plot}
plot_autocorrelation(a, group_by = "sample", lag_range = c(1, 500))
```

```{r acf-heatmap, fig.height=7}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_autocorrelation(a, "heatmap", group_by = "sample"))
```

Use `group_by = "cluster"` to summarize by the original Manhattan clusters;
this reads existing labels without fitting another clustering model.

```{r acf-manhattan-plot}
plot_autocorrelation(a, group_by = "cluster")
```

### Optional clustering of ACF profiles

The ACF method uses centered, unscaled PCA; correlation-distance neighbors;
a `uwot` fuzzy graph; and igraph Leiden clustering. UMAP coordinates are for
display. The independent ACF labels are zero-based and stored in `acf_cluster`.
The original `cluster` column retains the Manhattan labels.

```{r acf-clustering}
set.seed(123)
rng_before <- .Random.seed
acf_clustered <- locus_autocorrelation(x_leiden, max_lag = 500,
    clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = 50, n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0)
stopifnot(identical(rng_before, .Random.seed),
    identical(colData(acf_clustered)$cluster, colData(x_leiden)$cluster))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(acf_clustered)$acf_cluster_status)))
plot_autocorrelation(acf_clustered, group_by = "acf_cluster")
```

Reads with constant ACFs or insufficient usable information keep explicit
statuses. Unassigned reads are excluded from `acf_cluster` views but remain in
all/sample summaries and exports. Fewer than four valid reads cannot form an
ACF clustering fit.

### Check against the planted synthetic truth

Truth is joined **after** analysis, using sample and original read IDs.
It does not affect the ACFs or either clustering model. The strongest positive
local ACF peak in the 140–250-bp band should track the planted spacing.

```{r synthetic-checks}
truth <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "truth.tsv"))
cd <- as.data.frame(colData(acf_clustered))
key <- function(sample, read) paste(sample, read, sep = "::")
ix <- match(key(cd$sample_name, cd$original_RID), key(truth$sample_name, truth$original_RID))
stopifnot(!anyNA(ix), identical(as.integer(Matrix::colSums(assay(x_leiden))),
    as.integer(truth$n_calls[ix])))
cd$truth <- truth$truth[ix]
cd$period_bp <- truth$period_bp[ix]
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(planted = cd$truth, acf_cluster = cd$acf_cluster)))
peak_summary <- aggregate(positive_local_peak_140_250_bp ~ truth,
    data = cd[!is.na(cd$period_bp), ], FUN = median)
knitr::kable(peak_summary, digits = 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(cd$positive_local_peak_140_250_bp[!is.na(cd$period_bp)] -
    cd$period_bp[!is.na(cd$period_bp)]) <= 10))
```

Peak detection requires the complete band and a neighboring lag beyond it:
`max_lag >= 251`. A missing peak means no qualifying positive local maximum,
not a repeat length of zero. Peak agreement is the synthetic numerical check;
cluster identities can vary across dependency versions.

### Run either analysis, both, or neither from the same sample sheet

```{r independent-switches, eval=FALSE}
# Neither
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = FALSE)
# Manhattan Leiden only
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = FALSE)
# ACF only
analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = TRUE)
# Both, with separate settings for ACF clustering
both <- analyze_loci(samples, regions, clustering = TRUE, autocorrelation = TRUE,
    autocorrelation_options = list(max_lag = 500, clustering = TRUE,
        n_pcs = 50, n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0))
a <- metadata(both[[1]])$autocorrelation
metadata(both[[1]])$autocorrelation_status
```

A failed optional ACF computation warns and records a status while preserving
the locus and Manhattan fit. Check `autocorrelation_status` before using the
attached result. ACF graphs and metadata describe the original run; recompute
with `locus_autocorrelation(x_subset)` after subsetting a locus.

## Real LCL example: rs12470189 {#lcl}

This example uses the rank-1 locus in the native R workflow under
`code/clustering_methods/auto_correlation`. The saved default analysis is
**chr2:119290056–119292055**, a 2,000-bp window centered using the workflow's
rule around rs12470189 at position 119291056. Its cached input contains **255
phased reads from 15 contributing libraries** at the time this tutorial was
prepared. The code below reports actual counts on every run.

### Exact input selection and provenance

The LCL pipeline selects full-span reads with at least one m6A call and a
phased focal heterozygous genotype (`0|1` or `1|0`, HP1/HP2). A standard package
sample-sheet run retains all full-span reads, including zero-call and unphased
reads. Consequently, using the same locus and samples alone does **not**
reproduce the pipeline's read selection.

To demonstrate the exact current analysis, we reuse its read-only
`m6a_input.rds` cache and the accompanying selection signature. We convert only
the container orientation (reads × bases to bases × reads), preserve its read
order and phasing metadata, and recompute ACF with the package. We do not rerun
phasing or alter any saved LCL results. The real input files are not part of the
synthetic download. If the cache is missing, run your native R pipeline first.

```{r lcl-note, results='asis', echo=FALSE}
if (!params$run_lcl) cat("**LCL execution is disabled in this render.** Set `run_lcl: true` on a filesystem with the saved LCL inputs to execute the following chunks.\n")
```

### Load the existing run and create its sample sheet

```{r lcl-inputs, eval=params$run_lcl}
lcl_dir <- file.path(params$project, params$lcl_run)
selection_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "inputs", "selection_signature.rds")
input_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "inputs", params$lcl_region, "m6a_input.rds")
report_path <- file.path(lcl_dir, "outputs", params$lcl_region, "report_data.rds")
stopifnot(all(file.exists(c(selection_path, input_path, report_path))))
selection <- readRDS(selection_path)
input <- readRDS(input_path)
report <- readRDS(report_path)
r <- report$region
stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1L, identical(as.character(r$region_id), params$lcl_region),
    identical(rownames(input$binary), input$records$row_id),
    identical(input$records$row_id, report$row_ids),
    ncol(input$binary) == r$width,
    identical(as.integer(colnames(input$binary)), seq.int(r$analysis_start, r$analysis_end)))
cohort <- strsplit(r$contributing_samples, ",", fixed = TRUE)[[1]]
sm <- selection$sample_table[match(cohort, selection$sample_table$sample_name), ]
stopifnot(!anyNA(sm$sample_name), !anyDuplicated(sm$sample_name))
lcl_samples <- make_sample_sheet(data.frame(sample_name = sm$sample_name,
    sample_label = sub("_.*", "", sm$sample_name),
    m6a = file.path(sm$fire_dir, "extracted_results", "m6a_by_chr",
        paste0(sm$sample_name, ".ft_extracted_m6a.{chr}.bed.gz")),
    m6a_format = "bed12_fibertools"))
lcl_regions <- prepare_regions(data.frame(chr = r$chr,
    start = r$analysis_start - 1L, end = r$analysis_end, region_id = r$region_id),
    coordinate_system = "bed")
knitr::kable(data.frame(sample_name = cohort,
    retained_reads = as.integer(table(factor(input$records$sample_name, levels = cohort)))))
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = c("selection_signature.rds", "m6a_input.rds", "report_data.rds"),
    md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(c(selection_path, input_path, report_path)))))
```

This sample sheet can be used with either `analyze_loci()` switch. For a new
unfiltered extraction on the same samples and region, use the following call;
it is not the phased-cache analysis used for the comparison below:

```{r lcl-unfiltered-alternative, eval=FALSE}
lcl_all_full_span <- analyze_loci(lcl_samples, lcl_regions,
    clustering = FALSE, autocorrelation = TRUE,
    autocorrelation_options = list(clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = 50,
        n_neighbors = 10, resolution = 0.4, seed = 0))
```

### Convert the exact phased input to a locus experiment

```{r lcl-container, eval=params$run_lcl}
records <- input$records
stopifnot(all(records$sample_name %in% lcl_samples$sample_name),
    all(records$haplotype %in% c("HP1", "HP2")),
    all(records$focal_genotype %in% c("0|1", "1|0")),
    all(records$allele_status == "phased_focal_genotype"))
cd_lcl <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(records, row.names = records$row_id)
cd_lcl$RID <- records$row_id  # unique sample + molecule key used by the package
cd_lcl$sample_label <- lcl_samples$sample_label[
    match(records$sample_name, lcl_samples$sample_name)]
positions <- seq.int(r$analysis_start, r$analysis_end)
m <- Matrix::Matrix(t(input$binary), sparse = TRUE)
dimnames(m) <- list(paste(r$chr, positions, sep = ":"), records$row_id)
rr <- GRanges(r$chr, IRanges::IRanges(positions, width = 1L))
names(rr) <- rownames(m)
x_lcl <- SummarizedExperiment(assays = list(m6a = m), rowRanges = rr,
    colData = cd_lcl, metadata = list(region = lcl_regions, samples = lcl_samples,
        input_source = input_path, input_md5 = unname(tools::md5sum(input_path))))
stopifnot(identical(unname(as.matrix(assay(x_lcl))), unname(t(input$binary))))
knitr::kable(data.frame(reads = ncol(x_lcl), bases = nrow(x_lcl),
    samples = length(unique(colData(x_lcl)$sample_name))))
```

### Recompute native R ACF and independent ACF clusters

Use the saved run's settings rather than assuming its defaults. For the current
`resolution04` run these are 2,000 lag features (0–1999), 50 requested PCs,
10 neighbors, resolution 0.4, and seed 0.

```{r lcl-acf, eval=params$run_lcl}
p <- report$params
knitr::kable(data.frame(parameter = c("n_features", "n_pcs", "n_neighbors", "resolution", "seed"),
    value = unlist(p[c("n_features", "n_pcs", "n_neighbors", "resolution", "seed")], use.names = FALSE)))
lcl_acf <- locus_autocorrelation(x_lcl, max_lag = p$n_features - 1L,
    clustering = TRUE, n_pcs = p$n_pcs, n_neighbors = p$n_neighbors,
    resolution = p$resolution, seed = p$seed)
stopifnot(identical(dim(t(assay(lcl_acf))), dim(report$acf)),
    identical(unname(is.na(t(assay(lcl_acf)))), unname(is.na(report$acf))))
max_difference <- max(abs(t(assay(lcl_acf)) - report$acf), na.rm = TRUE)
stopifnot(max_difference < 1e-12)
knitr::kable(data.frame(check = "Maximum absolute ACF difference from saved native R run",
    value = max_difference))
knitr::kable(as.data.frame(table(status = colData(lcl_acf)$acf_cluster_status)))
```

This numerical comparison checks the same reads, base positions, lag count and
normalization. Cluster labels can vary with dependency versions; the ACF method
and package versions are recorded in `metadata(lcl_acf)$autocorrelation$clustering`.
The tutorial does not reinterpret HP1/HP2 as REF/ALT: that requires the saved
focal genotype and allele mapping. Existing allele labels remain in `colData`.

```{r lcl-acf-curves, eval=params$run_lcl}
plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, group_by = "acf_cluster", lag_range = c(1, 500))
```

```{r lcl-acf-heatmap, eval=params$run_lcl, fig.height=8}
ComplexHeatmap::draw(plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, "heatmap",
    group_by = "acf_cluster", lag_range = c(1, 500)))
```

```{r lcl-acf-sample, eval=params$run_lcl, fig.height=6}
plot_autocorrelation(lcl_acf, group_by = "sample", lag_range = c(1, 500))
```

## Export results

### Save the synthetic analyses separately

`write_locus_results()` preserves the original Manhattan analysis.
`write_autocorrelation_results()` saves the independent ACF experiment with
both label columns. Output directories must be new or empty.

```{r exports}
write_locus_results(leiden_results, file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-leiden"))
write_autocorrelation_results(acf_clustered, file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation"))
if (params$run_lcl)
    write_autocorrelation_results(lcl_acf, file.path(run_dir, "LCL-autocorrelation"))
knitr::kable(data.frame(file = list.files(file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation"))))
```

The ACF export contains `autocorrelation.rds`, `reads.tsv`, `lags.tsv`, mean/SD/SEM
tables, profile/heatmap PDFs, and `acf_edges.tsv` when clustering was requested.
For an `analyze_loci(..., autocorrelation = TRUE)` result, `write_locus_results()`
exports its attached ACF automatically under each locus's `autocorrelation/`
subdirectory. To reload a standalone ACF result:

```{r reload}
restored_acf <- readRDS(file.path(run_dir, "synthetic-autocorrelation", "autocorrelation.rds"))
stopifnot(identical(assay(restored_acf), assay(acf_clustered)),
          identical(colData(restored_acf), colData(acf_clustered)))
```
